title: Watch Jobs
markdown:
The **watch** module (`openexecutive.watch`) runs **watch jobs**: unattended ERPNext runs, defined in code, that read a fixed set of ERPNext data, apply rules in code and leave the principal notices. A job never runs the Executive's tool loop, never lets a model choose a read, and never writes a figure a model made up. Job draft cards (a Dunning, an invoice on hold) come with the jobs themselves; for now a job leaves notices only.

### The registry (`watch.registry`), code only

- A job is a `WatchJob(id, title, reads, build, schedule, card_cap_day, default_settings, reason_schema=None)`. Its id is oe_connector's `[a-z0-9-]{1,40}`, the key of the job's listing in `oe_connector_watch_jobs` and of its ERP user `oe-watch-<id>@<site>`.
- `reads` is a tuple of `WatchRead(tool, shape, arguments, label)`: an oe_connector tool, the shape of its arguments as oe_connector lists it (a fixed value matches exactly; a slot `$company`, `$date` (an ISO date within 400 days), `$party`, `$parties` / `$customers` (up to 50 names), `$int` (1–500) takes any value of its type; a `fields` list is the most a call may ask for; an object has exactly its keys), the code that builds the run's arguments from the settings and the day, and how a notice names it. Only `run_report` and `list_records` may be listed for now.
- `build(results, settings, today)` is pure code returning `CardSpec(key, summary, values, facts)`s; every figure comes from the results.
- `JOBS` is read-only and holds only what the module lists; nothing adds a job from settings, chat or an API. Phase 0 lists none (the test job, `watch.jobs._example`, is put in by the tests). `tests/unit/watch_job_vectors.json` pins the id pattern, slot names, shapes and one signed `watch` assertion against oe_connector.

### Settings (`watch.settings`, table `watch_jobs`)

One row per job: `enabled` (off by default), `settings` (JSON, exactly the job's `default_settings` keys and types, within the slot bounds), `configured_by_person_id` and `configured_at`, and an optional `reviewer_person_id`, stored for the jobs' later separation of duties and never read by the runner. Only the principal changes a row, through `PUT /watch/jobs/{id}` (a signed principal or local login's operator, `delegation.verified.caller_refusal`; 409 / 403 otherwise; see API Reference), which records who did it and writes a private `watch_job_configured` audit row. No chat action calls it. `ERPNEXT_WATCH_JOBS_ENABLED` (off) is the operator's master switch: off, no job runs whatever its row says.

### The marker and the gateway

Each read runs inside `erpnext_caller.watch_run(job, tool, arguments)`, a marker code sets and no tool can. It is bound to a job that is registered and on, one of the tools it lists, and the digest of the call's exact arguments, which must fit the read's shape. It is refused (`WatchRefused`, a reason code) while a turn's session is bound, while any other marker is set (the brief's, the oversight export's, the answer check's, a supplier's, a draft's, or another watch read's), and without `ERPNEXT_CALLER_PRIVATE_KEY` (`watch-needs-keys`): a job never takes the brief's unsigned service path. It saves the marker it found and puts it back on exit.

Inside it `caller_for` answers `ErpnextCaller("watch", job=<id>)` before any session logic, and only alone (with a session or another marker it refuses). `mint` signs `kind: "watch"` with `sub` the job's id, no email or supplier and never a `purpose`, and refuses any draft tool. The gateway refuses every other call inside the marker, ERPNext's or any server's (`outside-watch-read`), compares the arguments' digest after its own argument coercion, and re-checks at call time that no turn and no other marker is bound. Withheld tools stay refused.

oe_connector checks the job is listed and the call fits one of its listed reads, as the job's own narrow ERP user when the job is set `as_job_user`, else the OE Reader service view, and reports which in the result's top-level `acting` (`{kind, job, as_job_user, user}`). The runner reads only that top-level key: it records, per read, whether the read ran as the job's user (in `watch_runs.reads`, never the user's name), and ends the run when `acting.job` names another job. Nothing yet routes on it: every notice goes to the principal.

### The runner (`watch.runner`)

- **Once a day.** A scheduler tick hook (`maybe_run`) starts each job that is on, once it is past its hour in the company's time zone, when it wins the day's claim: a `watch_runs` row (`job`, `day`, `status`, `started_at`, `attempts`, `cards`, `error`, `reads`) taken under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. A run left `running` for 30 minutes is retried once, then failed. A day whose hour daylight saving skipped still runs. Each run is one task of its own, with no session and no audit scope, under the turn id `watch:<id>:<day>` and the job's cost budget once cost caps are in (`cost_caps.bind_job("watch:<id>")`, imported by name).
- **Reads.** Each read's arguments are built by the job's code and checked against its shape before the call. A refused or failed read (an error result, a plain-text refusal, a timeout, a marker refusal) ends the run: the principal gets one notice a day naming the read and why, in our words, and nothing partial is raised. The run's row, the log and the audit hold a reason code only, never ERPNext's text.
- **Rules.** `job.build` turns the results into findings.
- **Reasons** (a job with a `reason_schema`): one tool-less call to the fast utility model with its own constant system prompt (`REASON_SYSTEM`). Its input is the findings' facts, bounded (at most 20 findings, 8 facts each, 120 characters a value) and wrapped as untrusted, keyed by short ids (`f1`…), never the findings' keys. Its reply is kept only as a JSON object of reasons for the ids it was shown, each cleaned and at most 200 characters; anything else is dropped. A reason is labelled on the notice as a model's words, never as a figure, and never reaches a key, a title or routing. Usage is recorded under actor `watch:<id>`.
- **Notices.** Private alerts (source `watch`, `needs: fyi`, a severity code picks) stored directly (`alerts.store.insert_alert`), never through the alert pipeline's triage, whose model would store its own headline and body or drop the finding: tagged private and routed to the principal, whoever the stored reviewer is. The headline is code only (`notice_subject`: the job's title and counts); every ERPNext string in the body is stripped of control characters, line breaks, markdown and links, capped at about 120 characters, and the body is wrapped `wrap_untrusted(source="erpnext", author="watch:<id>")`. A run takes at most 200 findings from its rules, and `card_cap_day` counts attempts, not stored notices; a finding whose notice is still open (its dedupe key is a digest of the finding's key) isn't raised again.
- **Audit.** One private `watch_run` row per run: status, reason code and counts only.
